subject: QBR prep: Acme Retail health flags, renewal risks & exec attention needed
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-retail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Brandt <markus@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Preparing for next week's QBR — initial notes

Vanessa / team,

Thanks for scheduling the QBR for next Friday. Markus and I pulled a quick list of things we'd like you to priority on the deck:

- Recent latency spike last week on product-recommendation endpoints (saw 450ms p95 on 2/24).
- Requesting details on token-cost trends and any mitigation plans for our high-throughput campaigns.
- Confirmation of audit logs retention policy for our EU stores (we believe current retention is 30 days).

Can your team share the health snapshot and any renewal-related risk items ahead of time? We'll need that for our internal finance review.

Appreciate it — Alice

--
Alice Chen
Director, AI Integrations
Acme Retail
[Attachment: acme_request_note.txt (txt)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-retail.com>, Markus Brandt <markus@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Preparing for next week's QBR — initial notes

Hi Alice / Markus —

Thanks for the heads-up. We're assembling the QBR packet and will surface the items you flagged. Quick status:

- Latency spike: root cause was a mis-tuned autoscaler on the Dedicated pool for your EU shards. Mitigation: temporary capacity bump applied 2/25; longer-term autoscaler fix scheduled for rollout on 3/10.
- Token-cost trends: preliminary model-route optimization shaved estimated cost by ~12% in Feb; we'll include per-route breakdown.
- Audit logs retention: private deployment (EU) is currently at 30 days by default; we can enable 90-day retention under your enterprise plan — need PO confirmation.

I've attached the customer health snapshot and a draft renewal risk register for your review. Please flag anything that should be elevated to execs before the QBR.

Thanks —
Vanessa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme_health_snapshot_2027-03-01.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: acme_renewal_risk_register_20270301.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR prep: Acme Retail health flags, renewal risks & exec attention needed

Vanessa — quick notes after reviewing the snapshot and running the renewal risk register:

1) Risk tiering: I'm tagging three items as "high" that I think need exec awareness in the QBR slide:
   - Ongoing autoscaler flakiness for EU Dedicated pool (affects 12% of Acme traffic; repeat incidents in last 6 weeks).
   - Contract shortfall: Acme's committed monthly spend is trending down 18% vs. initial forecast — finance will press on commit during renewal.
   - Audit/retention asks: legal wants explicit SLA for log retention and access controls; current offering requires enterprise upgrade.

2) Proposed exec asks:
   - COO or VP of Sales to join the QBR for the renewal discussion (to confirm commercial flexibility).
   - Commitment date from runtime team for autoscaler fix (Karthik, can we commit to 3/10 rollout with validated perf metrics?).

3) Attachments: updated risk register (minor edits).

Ben
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme_renewal_risk_register_20270303.pdf (pdf)]

Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR prep: Acme Retail health flags, renewal risks & exec attention needed

Team — status update and final asks ahead of QBR deck cut tomorrow 3/5: 

- Autoscaler fix: engineering has validated the patch in staging (test window 2/28–3/2). We have a scheduled maintenance rollout to EU Dedicated on 3/10; however, to reduce immediate risk for the QBR we can schedule a controlled capacity resize during the QBR week (3/8) so Acme sees immediate guardrails. Confirm if you want that conservative approach.

- Commercial: Sales is prepared to offer a one-time billing credit tied to GA of the autoscaler fix; Ben, recommend we surface a "credit framework" slide (amount ranges) instead of exact numbers.

- Compliance/Retention: Legal confirmed OEM accounts need an enterprise addendum to extend logs to 90 days; we'll provide a template addendum for Acme to review post-QBR.

Action items (final):
1) Vanessa: finalize QBR slide deck with the two exec-flag slides (autoscaler incident summary + renewal ask/credit framework).
2) Ben: draft the commercial slide and talking points for VP/COO.
3) Laura: please attend the QBR to handle exec-level questions on SLAs; if not available, nominate an alternate.
4) Acme (Alice): confirm whether you'd like the immediate capacity resize on 3/8, or prefer to wait for the 3/10 rollout.

I'll be on standby during the QBR prep window and can join tomorrow's rehearsal at 10:00 PT.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
VP, Runtime & Reliability, Redwood Inference
